clause_name: RLA-470 — Residential Lease — Default Events and Notice or Cure
library_question: Do the standard material-default, nonpayment, notice, cure, and urgent-lawful-action provisions apply without acceleration or self-help?

blocks.text: A default occurs only when Tenant, an occupant, guest, invitee, animal, or Tenant's property materially fails to comply with a lawful Lease obligation or applicable tenant duty. A minor, technical, disputed, or nonmaterial issue is not automatically a material default. Every remedy remains subject to the notice, cure, service, fair housing, anti-retaliation, and court-process requirements of applicable law.

If Base Rent or another amount legally subject to the nonpayment remedy remains unpaid when due, Landlord may deliver a written notice that complies with K.S.A. 58-2564(b) and applicable service law. This Lease does not shorten the required payment period, expand permitted service methods, or authorize filing before the statutory period expires. A disputed fee or reimbursement will not be treated as grounds for an expedited nonpayment eviction unless that remedy is legally available on the established facts.

For material noncompliance other than nonpayment, Landlord may deliver a written notice specifying with reasonable factual detail the acts and omissions constituting the breach and stating that this Lease will terminate on a date not less than thirty (30) days after Tenant receives the notice if the breach is not remedied within fourteen (14) days. If Tenant adequately initiates a good-faith cure within the fourteen-day period, the Lease will not terminate on that notice. If the same or a similar breach occurs after the fourteen-day period, Landlord may deliver a second written notice terminating the Lease on a date not less than thirty (30) days after receipt, without another opportunity to cure, only to the extent permitted by K.S.A. 58-2564(a).

Violence, serious threats, substantial property damage, illegal activity, or another immediate danger may require emergency services, protective orders, injunctive relief, or another lawful expedited response. Nothing in this section creates a contractual immediate eviction or eliminates any notice, cure, service, or court procedure required by law. Landlord may use an expedited or no-cure remedy only when a specific current statute or court order authorizes that remedy on the established facts.
